findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:

1) The caulking to the right of the kitchen’s dish machine is separating. Reseal to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
2) The fans of the walk in cooler contain an accumulation of dust. Dust may travel to contamination nonfood and food contact surfaces.

findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw chicken being stored over raw ground beef in a cooler (to the left of the handwashing sink) in the Grill area of the facility. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the chicken to be stored on the bottom shelf, and notified staff that animal proteins should be stored so that items requiring higher internal temperatures for cooking are stored below other items (proteins requiring a lower internal temperature and ready to eat [RTE] foods). Ensure storage order education occurs with all food handlers on a routine basis.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 A cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Ensure staff are was using proper technique when washing their hands.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 The following were all observed in the walk-in cooler.
1. Three containers of chicken and wild rice soup (~2.5gal each) made today were observed with internal temperatures of 49F, 45F, and 43F within the liquid portion of the soup (meat, vegetables, and rice settled to bottom). Based on cooling log, soup was prepared in the morning, had an internal temperature of 132F at 8am, and reached 51F after 2hrs. Based on the time frame of initial prep, the soup was past the 6hr time frame for proper cooling. Soup at 49F was discarded. 
2. Baking sheet with cooked rice had surface and internal temperature of 53F-62F and 61F-75F respectively. Cook stated rice was prepared around 11:30am-12pm. The first two hours of the cooling time frame was past based on information provided. Rice was discarded.
3. Cooked, shredded chicken in a covered container was observed with an internal temperature of 66F-67F. Cook noted it was cool to the touch when shredded and made around the same time as rice. Temperature was not monitored during the process. Chicken was discarded at the discretion of PIC.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Dish machine sanitizer concentration was observed at 0ppm chlorine. A full bucket of sanitizer was observed connected to the machine. An air bubble was present, and product was not suctioning properly through the line. A call for service was made, and dishes were manually sanitized at the 3 part sink (200ppm quat) until the dish machine was repaired. A technician arrived for repairs during the inspection. Upon checking the chemical lines and priming the machine the sanitizer concentration was observed at 50-100ppm.
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain sanitizer at the dish machine to allow for proper sanitization of dishes, and use test strips to verify concentration of final rinse. 

Quat solution in one of the sani-buckets at the AL dining area was observed with a concentration of ~100ppm quat. New solution was prepared and observed at 200ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain quat solutions as directed by the label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Can openers were observed with buildup along the edge of the blades. Can openers had not been used during prep today. Both can openers were taken to the dish area to go through ware washing. 
Milkshake machine was observed with dried food splash on surfaces above mixing wands from the day prior. Proper cleaning and sanitizing of milkshake machine food contact surfaces was discussed. Manager noted the machine would be cleaned and sanitized by servers prior to being used today.
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Soda nozzle and diffuser at the server area soda machine were observed with mold buildup. Manager stated all nozzles and diffusers would be cleaned by servers prior to lunch time use.
Beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Date marks of 8/8 and 8/12 were observed on pre-cooked seafood and noodles in the bottom of the grill prep cooler. Both items were removed for discard. A pan of deli turkey in the bottom of the grill cooler was observed without a date mark. Turkey was just prepared and labeled with a proper date mark.
Open cartons of liquid egg whites and heavy whipping cream were observed without date marks in the bottom of the sauté cooler. Items were opened over the weekend and provided with proper date marks.  
Commercially processed and prepared, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, once opened and prepared if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Sani-bucket in the prep area was observed with a wiping cloth hanging over the edge and not properly submerged in sanitizer solution. Wiping cloth was placed in the solution for proper storage. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee did not change gloves after removing a soiled can opener from the prep area and returned to vegetable prep. Proper glove use was discussed, and gloves were changed before continuing further with prep. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Dust and/or debris accumulation were observed on outer surfaces of the dish machine (backside, top, and above curtains), up inside the ventilation hood over the dish machine, and on surfaces of the dish dryer. Clean these areas as needed to eliminate buildup of dust and debris.
Floor drain under the dirty dish drain board at the 3 part sink had buildup down inside. Clean the floor drain as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11 Emergency eye wash station was observed connected to the faucet of the handsink in the Care Center prep area. Removal of the eye wash station from the handsink was discussed during the 11/27/18 inspection (see general comments from that report). Maintenance removed the eye wash station during the inspection. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Soap dispenser at the Care Center prep handsink was without soap. Employee noted it needed new batteries but C batteries were not available to allow for proper function. A pump bottle of soap was placed at the handsink 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Surface above milkshake mixing wands and the mixing surface of one of the wands were soiled with dried milkshake splash on the machine at the AL service counter. All surfaces were to be cleaned and sanitized prior to next use. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Surfaces inside the main ice machine were starting to accumulate some mold on the ceiling in front of the metal baffle and on the area around the opening behind the baffle where ice comes. 
Also, surfaces up inside the shoots of the water/ice dispenser in the AL dining area had some general buildup. Cleaning frequency was discussed for ice machines. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Portions of cooked, cooled, and sliced turkey breast were observed with internal temperatures of 66F and 70F in the walkin cooler. Portions of turkey were tightly covered with foil in stainless steel pans. Turkey was cooked in the morning, finished around 10a, and placed in the walkin cooler during cooling process based on information provided. Turkey breasts were removed from the walkin cooler to be sliced in the afternoon prior to inspector's arrival. Temperature was not checked during the cooling process, so it was not possible to determine how quickly turkey breasts cooled and/or if they cooled properly. Portions of sliced turkey were placed in single layers on baking sheets in the walkin freezer to rapidly drop the temperature. Monitoring the time/temperature during cooling and prep processes were discussed. Proper/rapid reheat to 165F/above prior to evening service in Care Center was also discussed. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Multiple foods were in various stages of the cooling process in the walkin cooler.
Stuffing prepared prior to inspector's arrival was tightly covered with foil in stainless steel pans. Product was ~20 minutes into the cooling process based on information provided and had an internal temperature of 76F.
Marinara prepared from ambient temperature ingredients was ~1.5hrs into the cooling process in a covered, plastic 22qt container (~16qt of product) and had surface/internal temperatures at 55F/62F respectively.
A meat sauce prepared by combining ambient temperature, canned sauce with cooked, cooled ground beef was in a covered 22qt container (~16qt of product) and had an internal temperature of 50F.
Three portions of soup also in covered, plastic 22qt containers (~16qt of product in each) had internal temperatures at 51F-58F. 
Soups and sauces were placed in shallow pans (~4" deep) uncovered in the walkin freezer on speed racks, with ice wands also utilized in some products, to speed up the cooling process. Stuffing was also uncovered in the walkin freezer to finish rapid chill.  
Changes to the cooling process were discussed at length. Soups are currently monitored with a cooling chart but other products are not getting checked regularly. All cooling foods need to be monitored during the cooling process to ensure proper cooling. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4)
Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6)
Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. 
When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be:
(1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Plastic ice paddle used to knock ice loose in the main ice machine was stored on the top ledge of the machine next to the side air vent, which had dust accumulation on it. Ice paddle and extra ice scoop, which was also on top of the ice machine were taken to the dish area for ware washing. Storage options were discussed. 
Clean equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.
